# Publisher document rights review

<!-- Generated by models/generate.py from models/catalog.json. Edit the catalog, then run `python3 generate.py --write`. -->

Checked 2026-10-06. The repository's MIT license covers only its original work: digests, generated Markdown, and scripts. Publisher documents keep their own terms. A public URL is not permission to republish, and a model-weights license is not automatically a documentation license. This review is not legal advice.

Each of the 34 PDFs was searched on every page, and in its links and metadata, for a redistribution notice. None contains one. The decision therefore rests on the publisher's terms or on a license published with the document.

## Moonshot AI: why these copies are committed

Moonshot AI publishes Kimi K3's technical report in the [Kimi-K3 repository](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3) under the Kimi K3 License. That license defines the licensed "Software" to include "associated documentation" and permits anyone to copy, publish, and distribute it, provided the copyright and permission notice is included. An earlier revision of this catalog declined to rely on that grant because the license does not name the PDF. On re-review, the report is documentation published alongside the model in the same repository, so it falls within that definition. The license's other conditions concern model-as-a-service revenue and display in large commercial products and do not apply to this repository. The Kimi K2.7 Code model card is the README of Moonshot AI's Hugging Face repository, released under a Modified MIT License that likewise covers associated documentation files. Both license texts are committed beside the copies. Anyone who prefers explicit confirmation can write to `license@moonshot.ai`, the contact the Kimi K3 License names.

## Approval needed for the remaining documents

To commit any other PDF or its verbatim extraction, obtain written permission from its publisher that covers both the unmodified PDF and a complete verbatim Markdown extraction in this public repository, with attribution. Then:

1. Record the grant in `catalog.json`: set `rights` to `granted` and fill in `rights_basis`, `license_name`, `license_url`, `license_file`, and `license_sha256`.
2. Commit the permission or license text as `license_file` in the model folder.
3. Add `!<slug>/system-card.pdf` and `!<slug>/system-card.md` (or `!<slug>/model-card.md`) negations to `models/.gitignore`.
4. Run `python3 local_cards.py --model <slug>`, then `python3 generate.py --write --check`, and commit.
